holidays.name: Sesame Street Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the iconic children's show where furry monsters, a grouchy trash-can dweller, and a very patient bird teach kids their ABCs and 123s. Fans mark the day by watching old episodes and belting out the theme song.
holidays.origin: Sesame Street premiered on National Educational Television (the forerunner of PBS) on November 10, 1969, and fans have celebrated the anniversary ever since.
holidays.funFact: The show was designed after research suggested that young children were glued to TV commercials, so the creators borrowed the fast, catchy style of ads to teach letters and numbers.

holidays.name: Forget-Me-Not Day
holidays.description: A day for remembering the people and moments in your life that matter, named after the small blue flower that symbolizes remembrance. It is a good excuse to call an old friend or write a note to someone you haven't talked to in ages.
holidays.origin: The forget-me-not has long been a symbol of remembrance in European folklore, and informal observances using the flower have been held in various countries, with this date popular among unofficial holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Legend says a medieval knight fell into a river while picking the flowers for his lady, and as he was swept away he tossed them to her and cried out, 'Forget me not!'

holidays.name: Area 51 Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for conspiracy theorists, sci-fi fans, and curious folks who love to speculate about aliens, secret government hangars, and unexplained lights in the desert sky.
holidays.origin: Area 51 observances grew out of internet culture and the long-running fascination with the secretive Nevada Air Force facility, which was only officially acknowledged by the CIA in 2013.
holidays.funFact: A 2019 Facebook joke event called 'Storm Area 51, They Can't Stop All of Us' attracted over two million RSVPs, though only a small number of people actually showed up in Nevada.

holidays.name: Top Up Day
holidays.description: A day to put your money where your heart is by topping up a meaningful fund, whether that's your savings account, a travel jar, or a loved one's gift card. It's all about the satisfying feeling of refilling something that was running low.
holidays.origin: This quirky observance comes from the general internet-era tradition of unofficial days that encourage small, practical self-care acts like refilling accounts, supplies, and glasses of water.
holidays.funFact: Studies on personal finance habits suggest that small, regular top-ups to a savings account can add up faster than people expect, thanks to the power of consistency.

holidays.name: Plum Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day for the rich, boozy, fruit-packed steamed dessert that's famous for being lit on fire at the table. Despite the name, traditional plum pudding doesn't actually need to contain plums.
holidays.origin: Plum pudding dates back to medieval England, where 'plum' was used to describe any dried fruit such as raisins and currants. Over the centuries it became a classic Christmas dish, and its mid-November observance falls close to the traditional time for making the pudding ahead of the holidays.
holidays.funFact: In Victorian Britain, families often made the pudding on 'Stir-up Sunday' weeks in advance, and everyone in the household was supposed to take a turn stirring it and make a wish.
